extracted_information: The web content provides a detailed explanation of MemGPT, a virtual memory management system for Large Language Models (LLMs) developed by researchers at UC Berkeley.

llm_limitations.context_window_size_example: GPT-3 can only process 8192 tokens at a time.
llm_limitations.memory_issue: Short-term memory loss, similar to Dory from Finding Nemo.
llm_limitations.document_processing_limitation: Cannot process large documents; a typical novel may contain over 200,000 tokens, exceeding LLM context limits.

features.name: Long-term memory
features.description: Preserves information beyond a single context window, enabling retrieval of old chat history and document details.

features.name: Modular processing
features.description: Breaks down tasks into sub-routines and chains multiple functions together (e.g., searching archives, then sending a message).

features.name: Event-based control flow
features.description: Different events (user messages, scheduled tasks, new documents) trigger the LLM to make inferences and take actions.

features.name: Memory hierarchy
features.description: Two memory types: main context (like RAM) and external context (like disk storage). Information is moved between them using MemGPT's functions.

features.name: OS functions
features.description: Special functions to search databases, analyze documents modularly, rewrite responses based on user feedback, and more.

references.title: MemGPT: Giving Large Language Models Memory Management
